title: Introduction
content:
VPC endpoints VPC endpoints are virtual devices. They are horizontally scaled, redundant, and highly available VPC components. They allow communication between your compute resources and AWS services without imposing availability risks. Compute resources running in VPC can access Amazon S3 using a Gateway endpoint. PrivateLink interface endpoints can be used by compute resources running in VPC or on-premises. Workshop overview In this workshop, you will use two VPCs.
“VPC Cloud” is for cloud resources such as a Gateway endpoint and an EC2 instance to test with. “VPC On-Prem” simulates an on-premises environment such as a factory or corporate datacenter. An EC2 instance running strongSwan VPN software has been deployed in “VPC On-prem” and automatically configured to establish a Site-to-Site VPN tunnel with AWS Transit Gateway. This VPN simulates connectivity from an on-premises location to the AWS cloud. To minimize costs, only one VPN instance is provisioned to support this workshop. When planning VPN connectivity for your production workloads, AWS recommends using multiple VPN devices for high availability.

title: Project Proposal
content:
Enterprise Financial Data Lakehouse & Serverless Analytics Platform on AWS Scalable, Multi-Tier Financial Data Lakehouse & High-Performance Serverless Analytics Engine on AWS Cloud Project Lead & Solutions Architect: Nguyen Trung Hieu
Professional Role: Lead Cloud Architect & Finance Analytics Engineer
Program Track: First Cloud Applied Journey (FCAJ) – AWS Cloud Internship Portfolio
1. Executive Summary The project “Enterprise Financial Data Lakehouse & Serverless Analytics Platform on AWS” is designed to establish an enterprise-grade, cost-optimized, and highly secure cloud analytics foundation tailored for quantitative finance and risk analytics in Vietnam’s capital market.
Targeting financial institutions, brokerage firms, and investment funds, the platform addresses the challenge of ingesting, transforming, storing, and analyzing high-dimensional financial time-series data spanning 2017 to 2025. This encompasses trading data from 26 commercial banking stocks listed on HOSE/HNX/UPCoM, the VN-Index benchmark, and macroeconomic indicators (USD/VND exchange rates, overnight interbank rates). The platform integrates an end-to-end quantitative feature engineering pipeline computing 18 point-in-time features with Zero Look-Ahead Bias, facilitates Basel III regulatory tail-risk analytics ($VaR_{99%}$ and $ES_{97.5%}$), serves sub-10ms queries for algorithmic applications, and delivers executive visual insights via Business Intelligence dashboards.
Engineered strictly under the AWS Well-Architected Framework, the architecture leverages serverless and managed cloud-native paradigms within an isolated Multi-AZ Custom VPC. Operating on a pay-as-you-go financial model, the total projected infrastructure cost is under $10 USD/month, safely preserving the allocated $100 USD AWS Credit grant throughout the 12-week internship cycle.
2. Problem Statement & Return on Investment (ROI) The Business & Technical Challenge Data Silos & High Infrastructure Overhead: Traditional on-premises relational databases struggle to maintain decades of daily and intraday financial time series without costly SAN storage expansion and high database licensing fees. Performance Bottlenecks & Cost Inefficiencies: Querying financial features or computing regulatory tail-risk metrics across wide denormalized tables necessitates frequent full-table scans, resulting in severe latency and excessive computational waste. Regulatory Compliance & Data Exfiltration Risks: Financial data demands stringent zero-trust governance. Unrestricted public endpoints, long-lived hardcoded IAM credentials, and unencrypted transmission violate central banking guidelines (SBV Circular 41/2016 and Circular 13/2018). The AWS Cloud-Native Solution Medallion 3-Tier Lakehouse Architecture: Built upon Amazon S3 (Bronze $\to$ Silver $\to$ Gold) using compressed columnar Apache Parquet (Snappy) partitioned by year and ticker, slashing analytical query scan volume by over 85%. Serverless SQL Engine with Amazon Athena (Engine v3): Eliminates idle compute capacity by charging exclusively per data scanned ($5.00/TB), combined with CTAS table optimization. Sub-10ms Serving with Amazon DynamoDB: Decouples analytical batch data from low-latency online feature serving via a specialized Single-Table design. Perimeter Defense with AWS PrivateLink: Replaces public internet paths with private S3 Gateway VPC Endpoints, completely removing NAT Gateway data processing fees while guaranteeing in-transit data confinement. Return on Investment (ROI) & FinOps Efficiency Infrastructure Savings: Compared to traditional fixed-capacity data warehouses costing $150–$300 USD/month, the AWS Serverless architecture operates on demand, averaging only $0.25–$0.30 USD/day (~ $8.50–$9.50 USD/month). Time-to-Delivery: Fully managed services (AWS Glue, Athena, DynamoDB, QuickSight) compress data infrastructure onboarding time from months to weeks. 3. Target Solution Architecture The platform architecture spans four isolated functional tiers fully encapsulated within Amazon VPC:

Technical Component Design 4.1. Security, Identity & Network Fabric Amazon VPC Network Design: Built on top of the Multi-AZ Custom VPC deployed in Week 4 (10.10.0.0/16), isolating compute workloads across 2 Private Subnets while managing edge communication via 2 Public Subnets. IAM Identity Governance: Enforces Least Privilege access utilizing IAM Identity Center (SSO). Dedicated IAM Service Roles (FCAJ-EC2-Ingestion-Role, FCAJ-Glue-ETL-Role) replace long-lived static access keys. Private Data Perimeter: Communication between private compute resources and S3 buckets is routed exclusively through S3 Gateway VPC Endpoints, neutralizing external data theft vectors. 4.2. Medallion Lakehouse & Serverless ETL Layer Inheriting the verified star schema from the quantitative finance data model:
Bronze Zone (s3://fcaj-financial-datalake-raw/): Raw financial time series of 26 Vietnamese banking equities and macroeconomic indicators (2017–2025). Silver Zone (s3://fcaj-financial-datalake-processed/): AWS Glue Crawlers automatically catalog metadata into the Glue Data Catalog. Serverless PySpark ETL jobs cleanse, deduplicate, and convert datasets into Apache Parquet with Snappy compression, partitioned by year=YYYY/ticker=XXXX. Gold Zone (s3://fcaj-financial-datalake-curated/): Stores the normalized Feature Store comprising 18 point-in-time features lagged by $t-1$ (GARCH volatility, Garman-Klass, Parkinson, RSI, MACD, interbank rates). Houses the Basel III Tail-Risk Mart containing 94,311 empirical $VaR_{99%}$ and $ES_{97.5%}$ out-of-sample forecasts and violation classification records. 4.3. High-Speed Serving & Analytical Query Fabric Serverless Analytics with Amazon Athena: Employs CTAS and Partition Projection to optimize query performance and cut cloud billing costs when analyzing historical systemic stress events (2020 COVID shock, 2022 liquidity crisis). Sub-10ms Feature Serving with Amazon DynamoDB: Single-Table design using Partition Key TICKER#<symbol> and Sort Key DATE#<date_key>, augmented with a Global Secondary Index (GSI1) for querying cross-sectional sector metrics in a single network round-trip. 4.4. Executive Business Intelligence Amazon QuickSight: Direct connection to Athena Data Lake without intermediary warehouse staging. Interactive executive dashboard featuring backtesting validation curves, Basel regulatory traffic-light indicators, and risk factor attribution views. 5. Connect to EC2 with session manager For this workshop, you will use AWS Session Manager to access several EC2 instances. Session Manager is a fully managed AWS Systems Manager capability that allows you to manage your Amazon EC2 instances and on-premises virtual machines (VMs) through an interactive one-click browser-based shell. Session Manager provides secure and auditable instance management without the need to open inbound ports, maintain bastion hosts, or manage SSH keys.
First Cloud AI Journey Lab for indepth understanding of Session manager.

title: Access S3 from on-premises
content:
Overview In this section, you will create an Interface endpoint to access Amazon S3 from a simulated on-premises environment. The Interface endpoint will allow you to route to Amazon S3 over a VPN connection from your simulated on-premises environment.
Why using Interface endpoint:
Gateway endpoints only work with resources running in the VPC where they are created. Interface endpoints work with resources running in VPC, and also resources running in on-premises environments. Connectivty from your on-premises environment to the cloud can be provided by AWS Site-to-Site VPN or AWS Direct Connect. Interface endpoints allow you to connect to services powered by AWS PrivateLink. These services include some AWS services, services hosted by other AWS customers and partners in their own VPCs (referred to as PrivateLink Endpoint Services), and supported AWS Marketplace Partner services. For this workshop, we will focus on connecting to Amazon S3.

title: On-premises DNS Simulation
content:
AWS PrivateLink endpoints have a fixed IP address in each Availability Zone where they are deployed, for the life of the endpoint (until it is deleted). These IP addresses are attached to Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs). AWS recommends using DNS to resolve the IP addresses for endpoints so that downstream applications use the latest IP addresses when ENIs are added to new AZs, or deleted over time.
In this section, you will create a forwarding rule to send DNS resolution requests from a simulated on-premises environment to a Route 53 Private Hosted Zone. This section leverages the infrastructure deployed by CloudFormation in the Prepare the environment section.

title: Worklog Week 5
content:

- Verify the Ingestion Worker State Machine lifecycle. Completed Disaster remediation via SSM Session Manager and User Data injection. Implementation Details & Console Evidence: 1. Ingestion Worker Lifecycle State Machine The end-to-end operational lifecycle from cold provisioning to ingestion-ready state is governed by a strict deterministic state machine:
stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Provisioning: CloudFormation Deploy Provisioning --> Bootstrapping: EC2 Running (IMDSv2 Enforced) Bootstrapping --> VolumeAttaching: Run User Data to Install Python & CLI VolumeAttaching --> Formatting: Attach 20GB gp3 EBS Volume (/dev/xvdf) Formatting --> Mounting: Format XFS & Discover UUID (blkid) Mounting --> State_Ready: Write to /etc/fstab (nofail flag) & mount -a State_Ready --> Ingesting: Fetch Market Ticker Time-Series (Vnstock/Yahoo) Ingesting --> StagingSaved: Write Raw Ingestion Batches to /data/staging StagingSaved --> State_Ready: Batch Complete / Awaiting Next Pipeline Run State_Ready --> Stopped: Stop Instance (FinOps Guardrail) 2. IMDSv2 Enforcement: Mandatory session-oriented token requirement (HttpTokens: required, HttpPutResponseHopLimit: 1) to eliminate SSRF attack vectors against IAM instance credentials. Zero-Inbound Security Group: The associated Security Group has zero ingress rules (Inbound Rules: []), completely sealing the private subnet workload from external network reconnaissance. 3. EBS gp3 Staging Volume Management & Idempotent Mounting The dedicated 20GB gp3 cache volume is formatted with the high-throughput XFS filesystem. The automation script scripts/week5_mount_ebs.sh ensures idempotent execution across machine restarts:
# Retrieve filesystem UUID FS_UUID=$(blkid -s UUID -o value /dev/xvdf) # Create mount directory mkdir -p /data/staging # Register persistent mount entry with nofail flag echo "UUID=${FS_UUID} /data/staging xfs defaults,nofail 0 2" >> /etc/fstab # Mount all filesystems mount -a Storage Inspection Output (lsblk & df -h):

If the staging volume is detached or encounters transient hardware timeouts, the host OS continues booting without hanging in maintenance emergency mode.
4. Disaster Recovery Simulation: Key Pair Loss Remediation In enterprise production environments, loss of an administrative SSH private key (.pem) is an operational risk. Two standardized recovery procedures were validated:
Option 1: Keyless Remediation via AWS Systems Manager (Recommended) With the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore profile bound at launch, administrators initiate an authenticated shell session directly from the AWS Console or AWS CLI without opening port 22: aws ssm start-session --target <Worker-Instance-ID> Once connected, administrators easily append a replacement public key into ~/.ssh/authorized_keys. title: VPC Endpoint Policies
content:
When you create an interface or gateway endpoint, you can attach an endpoint policy to it that controls access to the service to which you are connecting. A VPC endpoint policy is an IAM resource policy that you attach to an endpoint. If you do not attach a policy when you create an endpoint, AWS attaches a default policy for you that allows full access to the service through the endpoint.
You can create a policy that restricts access to specific S3 buckets only. This is useful if you only want certain S3 Buckets to be accessible through the endpoint.
In this section you will create a VPC endpoint policy that restricts access to the S3 bucket specified in the VPC endpoint policy.
Connect to an EC2 instance and verify connectivity to S3 Start a new AWS Session Manager session on the instance named Test-Gateway-Endpoint. From the session, verify that you can list the contents of the bucket you created in Part 1: Access S3 from VPC: aws s3 ls s3://\<your-bucket-name\> The bucket contents include the two 1 GB files uploaded in earlier.
Create a new S3 bucket; follow the naming pattern you used in Part 1, but add a ‘-2’ to the name. Leave other fields as default and click create Successfully create bucket
Navigate to: Services > VPC > Endpoints, then select the Gateway VPC endpoint you created earlier. Click the Policy tab. Click Edit policy. The default policy allows access to all S3 Buckets through the VPC endpoint.
In Edit Policy console, copy & Paste the following policy, then replace yourbucketname-2 with your 2nd bucket name. This policy will allow access through the VPC endpoint to your new bucket, but not any other bucket in Amazon S3. Click Save to apply the policy. { "Id": "Policy1631305502445", "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Sid": "Stmt1631305501021", "Action": "s3:*", "Effect": "Allow", "Resource": [ "arn:aws:s3:::yourbucketname-2", "arn:aws:s3:::yourbucketname-2/*" ], "Principal": "*" } ] } Successfully customize policy
From your session on the Test-Gateway-Endpoint instance, test access to the S3 bucket you created in Part 1: Access S3 from VPC aws s3 ls s3://<yourbucketname> This command will return an error because access to this bucket is not permitted by your new VPC endpoint policy:
Return to your home directory on your EC2 instance cd~ Create a file fallocate -l 1G test-bucket2.xyz Copy file to 2nd bucket aws s3 cp test-bucket2.xyz s3://<your-2nd-bucket-name> This operation succeeds because it is permitted by the VPC endpoint policy.
Then we test access to the first bucket by copy the file to 1st bucket aws s3 cp test-bucket2.xyz s3://<your-1st-bucket-name> This command will return an error because access to this bucket is not permitted by your new VPC endpoint policy.
Part 3 Summary: In this section, you created a VPC endpoint policy for Amazon S3, and used the AWS CLI to test the policy. AWS CLI actions targeted to your original S3 bucket failed because you applied a policy that only allowed access to the second bucket you created. AWS CLI actions targeted for your second bucket succeeded because the policy allowed them. These policies can be useful in situations where you need to control access to resources through VPC endpoints.

title: Worklog Week 8: Automated ETL Pipelines with AWS Glue
content:
Week 8 Objectives: Construct a centralized metadata repository using AWS Glue Data Catalog across 3 logical databases: fcaj_bronze_db, fcaj_silver_db, and fcaj_gold_db. Deploy automated AWS Glue Crawlers with schema evolution controls (UPDATE_IN_DATABASE, DEPRECATE_IN_DATABASE) to infer schemas and discover Hive-style partitions (year=YYYY/ticker=XXXX). Author and schedule distributed Serverless PySpark ETL Jobs on AWS Glue (G.1X workers) converting raw CSV/JSON Lines into compressed Apache Parquet (Snappy), reducing storage footprint by >70%. Enforce the mathematical Zero Look-Ahead Bias principle across all 18 quantitative market risk features by applying PySpark window functions lagged strictly at $t-1$ and freezing In-Sample scalers. Weekly Task Execution Matrix: Day Technical Task Status Architecture Notes Mon - Define Glue Catalog database schemas for Bronze, Silver, and Gold zones.
- Package CloudFormation template iac/week8-glue-infrastructure.yaml. Completed Database isolation and IAM service role permissions configured. Tue - Configure and execute Glue Crawlers (fcaj-bronze-crawler, fcaj-silver-crawler).
- Validate partition discovery and data type inference. Completed Automatic discovery of Hive partitions: year and ticker. Wed - Develop PySpark ETL Job 1: Bronze to Silver (deduplication, date alignment, log return).
- Develop PySpark ETL Job 2: Silver to Gold Feature Store (18 features at $t-1$ lag). Completed PySpark Window specifications enforce rowsBetween(-21, -1) and lag(1). Thu - Execute Glue Job runs with Job Bookmarks enabled; monitor execution metrics in CloudWatch.
- Verify Parquet Snappy output files in S3 Silver and Gold buckets. Completed DPU execution time: 4.8 minutes; zero data leakage validated. Architecture & Data Lineage: flowchart TD subgraph S3_BRONZE ["S3 Bronze Zone (Raw)"] RAW_EOD["raw/market_prices/{ticker}/<br/>(OHLCV Daily CSV)"] RAW_MACRO["raw/macro_fx/<br/>(USDVND, Interbank Rates)"] end subgraph GLUE_CATALOG ["AWS Glue Data Catalog"] DB_BRONZE["<b>fcaj_bronze_db</b><br/>bronze_raw_market_prices<br/>bronze_raw_macro_rates"] DB_SILVER["<b>fcaj_silver_db</b><br/>silver_market_prices<br/>silver_fact_feature_store"] DB_GOLD["<b>fcaj_gold_db</b><br/>gold_fact_risk_forecasts<br/>gold_fact_backtest_summary"] end subgraph GLUE_ENGINE ["AWS Glue Serverless Spark (G.1X Workers)"] JOB1["<b>Job 1: Bronze -> Silver</b><br/>• Schema validation & deduplication<br/>• Forward-fill macro rates<br/>• Compute log return: rt = ln(Pt/Pt-1)"] JOB2["<b>Job 2: Silver -> Gold Features</b><br/>• 18 features via Windowing at t-1 lag<br/>• Parkinson & Garman-Klass volatility<br/>• Amihud illiquidity & Rolling skewness<br/>• <b>Zero Look-Ahead Bias Enforced</b>"] end subgraph S3_OUTPUT ["S3 Partitioned Lakehouse"] S3_SILVER["<b>S3 Silver Bucket</b><br/>processed/market_prices/<br/>Snappy Parquet<br/>year=YYYY/ticker=XXXX/"] S3_GOLD["<b>S3 Gold Bucket</b><br/>curated/feature_store/<br/>curated/risk_forecasts/<br/>Parquet CTAS Optimized"] end RAW_EOD --> DB_BRONZE RAW_MACRO --> DB_BRONZE DB_BRONZE --> JOB1 JOB1 --> S3_SILVER S3_SILVER --> DB_SILVER DB_SILVER --> JOB2 JOB2 --> S3_GOLD S3_GOLD --> DB_GOLD Implementation Details & PySpark ETL Script: PySpark Feature Engineering Enforcing Zero Look-Ahead Bias (scripts/glue_silver_to_gold_features.py) import sys from awsglue.transforms import * from awsglue.utils import getResolvedOptions from pyspark.context import SparkContext from awsglue.context import GlueContext from awsglue.job import Job from pyspark.sql import functions as F from pyspark.sql.window import Window sc = SparkContext() glueContext = GlueContext(sc) spark = glueContext.spark_session job = Job(glueContext) # Read cleansed Silver market prices df_silver = spark.read.parquet("s3://fcaj-financial-silver-ACCOUNT-REGION/processed/market_prices/") # Define Window Specifications strictly ending at t-1 (Zero Look-Ahead Bias) w_ticker = Window.partitionBy("ticker").orderBy("date_key") w_21d_t1 = Window.partitionBy("ticker").orderBy("date_key").rowsBetween(-21, -1) w_60d_t1 = Window.partitionBy("ticker").orderBy("date_key").rowsBetween(-60, -1) # 1. First-order lagged log return df_features = df_silver.withColumn("ret_log_t1", F.lag("log_return", 1).over(w_ticker)) # 2. Historical 21-day realized volatility lagged df_features = df_features.withColumn("realized_vol_21d", F.stddev("log_return").over(w_21d_t1)) # 3. Parkinson extreme high-low volatility lagged df_features = df_features.withColumn( "parkinson_sq", (F.log(F.col("high_price") / F.col("low_price")) ** 2) / (4.0 * 0.69314718) ) df_features = df_features.withColumn("parkinson_vol", F.sqrt(F.avg("parkinson_sq").over(w_21d_t1))) # 4. Amihud illiquidity ratio lagged df_features = df_features.withColumn( "amihud_raw", (F.abs(F.col("log_return")) / (F.col("volume") * F.col("close_price"))) * 1000000.0 ) df_features = df_features.withColumn("amihud_illiquidity", F.lag("amihud_raw", 1).over(w_ticker)) # 5. Rolling 60-day return skewness and kurtosis lagged df_mean_60 = F.avg("log_return").over(w_60d_t1) df_std_60 = F.stddev("log_return").over(w_60d_t1) df_norm = (F.col("log_return") - df_mean_60) / df_std_60 df_features = df_features.withColumn("skewness_60d", F.avg(df_norm ** 3).over(w_60d_t1)) df_features = df_features.withColumn("kurtosis_60d", F.avg(df_norm ** 4).over(w_60d_t1)) # Write curated Gold feature store partitioned by year df_features.write \ .mode("overwrite") \ .partitionBy("year") \ .parquet("s3://fcaj-financial-gold-ACCOUNT-REGION/curated/feature_store/") job.commit() Verification Method & Live Test Commands: Verify Glue Catalog Table Schemas:

python3 -c " import pyarrow.parquet as pq table = pq.read_table('s3://fcaj-financial-gold-ACCOUNT-REGION/curated/feature_store/year=2025/') df = table.to_pandas() # Confirm that ret_log_t1 at index i equals log_return at index i-1 for ticker VCB vcb = df[df['ticker']=='VCB'].sort_values('date_key').reset_index(drop=True) assert (vcb['ret_log_t1'].iloc[1:] == vcb['log_return'].iloc[:-1]).all(), 'Look-ahead bias detected!' print('Zero look-ahead bias validation: PASSED!') DDL with Partition Projection Configuration CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS fcaj_silver_db.fact_market_prices ( date_key INT, asset_id INT, open_price DOUBLE, high_price DOUBLE, low_price DOUBLE, close_price DOUBLE, volume BIGINT, log_return DOUBLE ) PARTITIONED BY (year INT, ticker STRING) STORED AS PARQUET LOCATION 's3://fcaj-financial-silver-ACCOUNT-REGION/processed/market_prices/' TBLPROPERTIES ( 'projection.enabled' = 'true', 'projection.year.type' = 'integer', 'projection.year.range' = '2018,2026', 'projection.ticker.type' = 'enum', 'projection.ticker.values' = 'VCB,BID,CTG,TCB,MBB,ACB,VPB,HDB,STB,VIB,SHB,TPB,LPB,MSB,OCB,EIB,SSB,NAB,BAB,BVB,KLB,PGB,SGB,NVB,ABB,VBB,PORTFOLIO', 'storage.location.template' = 's3://fcaj-financial-silver-ACCOUNT-REGION/processed/market_prices/year=${year}/ticker=${ticker}/' ); 2. Fissler-Ziegel Joint Loss Function View (vw_fissler_ziegel_loss) CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW fcaj_gold_db.vw_fissler_ziegel_loss AS SELECT f.date_key, d.full_date, a.ticker, m.model_code, f.var_forecast AS var_99, f.es_forecast AS es_975, -f.realized_return AS actual_loss, -- Fissler-Ziegel strictly consistent joint scoring function at alpha = 0.025 ( (CASE WHEN -f.realized_return > f.var_forecast THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) * (-f.realized_return - f.var_forecast) / (0.025 * f.es_forecast) ) + (f.var_forecast / f.es_forecast) + LN(f.es_forecast) - 1.0 AS fz_loss FROM "fcaj_gold_db"."fact_risk_forecasts" f JOIN "fcaj_gold_db"."dim_date" d ON f.date_key = d.date_key JOIN "fcaj_gold_db"."dim_asset" a ON f.asset_id = a.asset_id JOIN "fcaj_gold_db"."dim_model" m ON f.model_id = m.model_id; 3. Basel III Traffic Light Regulatory View (vw_basel_traffic_light) CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW fcaj_gold_db.vw_basel_traffic_light AS SELECT ticker, model_code, COUNT(*) AS total_test_days, SUM(CASE WHEN actual_loss > var_99 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS violation_count, ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN actual_loss > var_99 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE) / COUNT(*) * 100, 2) AS violation_rate_pct, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN actual_loss > var_99 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) <= 4 THEN 'GREEN (k=3.00)' WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN actual_loss > var_99 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) BETWEEN 5 AND 9 THEN 'YELLOW (k=3.40-3.85)' ELSE 'RED (k=4.00 Rejected)' END AS basel_zone FROM "fcaj_gold_db"."vw_fissler_ziegel_loss" WHERE full_date >= DATE '2024-01-01' GROUP BY ticker, model_code; Verification Method & Live Test Commands: Verify Athena Workgroup Safeguard via AWS CLI:

aws athena start-query-execution \ --work-group fcaj-risk-analytics-workgroup \ --query-string "SELECT ticker, AVG(fz_loss) FROM fcaj_gold_db.vw_fissler_ziegel_loss WHERE model_code='GJR_HANSEN' GROUP BY ticker;" \ --query-execution-context Database=fcaj_gold_db # Result: Execution time: 740ms; Data Scanned: 4.2 MB (vs 38 MB on unpartitioned CSV) # Scan volume reduction: 88.9% Verify Empirical Grand Tournament Champions:

Python Boto3 High-Performance Ingestion & Query Script (scripts/week10_feature_store_client.py) import boto3 import time from boto3.dynamodb.conditions import Key dynamodb = boto3.resource('dynamodb', region_name='ap-southeast-1') table = dynamodb.Table('FinancialFeatureStore') def get_single_bank_feature_vector(ticker: str, date_key: str): """Point-lookup for Treasury Desk pre-trade risk limit check (Latency target: <10ms).""" t0 = time.perf_counter() response = table.get_item( Key={ 'PK': f'TICKER#{ticker}', 'SK': f'DATE#{date_key}' }, ConsistentRead=True ) latency_ms = (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000.0 item = response.get('Item') return item, latency_ms def get_cross_sectional_market_slice(date_key: str): """Retrieve risk feature vectors for all 26 commercial banks in a single query.""" t0 = time.perf_counter() response = table.query( IndexName='GSI1', KeyConditionExpression=Key('GSI1-PK').eq(f'DATE#{date_key}') ) latency_ms = (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000.0 items = response.get('Items', []) return items, latency_ms if __name__ == '__main__': # Test point-lookup for Vietcombank (VCB) item, lat = get_single_bank_feature_vector('VCB', '20251231') print(f"Point-Lookup VCB Latency: {lat:.2f} ms | RetLogT1: {item.get('ret_log_t1') if item else 'N/A'}") # Test cross-sectional sector query items, lat_mkt = get_cross_sectional_market_slice('20251231') print(f"Sector Query Latency: {lat_mkt:.2f} ms | Total Banks Retrieved: {len(items)}") Verification Method & Live Test Commands: Verify Table Status and GSI1 Health:
